title: Booking a workshop
intro: Maya calls to ask about a photography workshop.
dialogue: Hello, I'd like to join the photography workshop. Is it still on Saturday morning?
We've moved it to Sunday because the room is needed for another event. It starts at ten thirty in the morning.
Is it in the main hall? That's where my last workshop was.
This time, go to Room Four on the first floor. The main hall will be closed.
How much does it cost, and what should I bring?
It costs twelve pounds. Bring a notebook. You can borrow a camera when you arrive.

title: Volunteering at a community garden
intro: Asha asks what to expect on her first day as a garden volunteer.
dialogue: I'm joining the garden volunteers on Saturday. Should I meet everyone at the main gate?
Use the side entrance on Mill Road. The main gate opens later. We'll meet beside the greenhouse at nine fifteen.
That's next week. This time we're clearing the paths. We have spare gloves, but please wear sturdy shoes.
We finish at eleven thirty, so you won't need lunch. Drinking water is available, but please bring a refillable bottle.

title: Hiring a bicycle
intro: A visitor plans to hire a bicycle for a ride along the river.
dialogue: I'd like to hire a bicycle for Friday. Would I need it for the whole day to ride along the river?
Four hours is usually enough. The half-day hire costs sixteen pounds. A full day costs twenty-eight.
Is a helmet included, or do I pay for one separately?
The helmet is included. A basket costs two pounds extra, but most people don't need one.
Can I collect the bike from your shop by the bridge?
That shop is being repaired. Collect it from our kiosk beside the railway station. If you book online, show us your confirmation email at the kiosk.

title: Changes to a museum tour
intro: A museum guide explains changes to the afternoon tour.
dialogue: Welcome to the Harbour Museum. Today's guided tour begins at two fifteen, a quarter of an hour later than advertised.
Please meet by the large clock in the entrance hall. The café will be busy, so don't wait there.
We'll begin with the model ships. The map gallery is closed, but we'll visit the old radio room instead.
You may take photographs in most rooms. Please put your camera away in the radio room, where some items are on loan.
The tour lasts about forty minutes. Afterwards, you can collect a free activity sheet from reception.

title: Asking about a room to rent

title: Planning a student research project
intro: Two students discuss how to collect information for a class project.
dialogue: For our project on campus travel, I thought we could interview students in the library.
We'd miss people who leave straight after class. Let's put a short online questionnaire on the class forum instead.
Good idea. We can ask how they travel and how long the journey takes. Should we ask for their home addresses?
No, we only need their travel time. We can also ask what would make them change how they travel.
I'll draft the questions by Thursday. Can you ask three classmates to try them before we post the final version?
Yes. And when we present the findings, let's use a bar chart to compare the most common forms of transport.

title: Visiting a wetland reserve
intro: A ranger briefs visitors before a walk around a wetland reserve.
dialogue: Today we are taking the short loop because the eastern path is flooded. The loop should take about fifty minutes.
At the first junction, keep left towards the wooden bridge. The right-hand path is for staff vehicles.
Please speak quietly near the viewing shelter. Sudden noise may frighten the birds away before everyone has seen them.
You can borrow binoculars from the visitor centre. There is no charge, but leave your name at the desk.
We'll end the walk at the picnic area. If you want to return to the car park, follow the blue signs from there.

questions.explanation: The ranger explains that flooding has made the eastern path unavailable.

questions.explanation: They should keep left towards the wooden bridge.

title: Reducing waste at a food market
intro: A market manager explains the results of a small waste reduction trial.
dialogue: We began by weighing the food left at the end of each market day. Bread made up the largest share, although we had expected vegetables to come first.
We offered vendors two options: sell surplus items at a lower price in the last hour, or set them aside for collection by a community kitchen.
At first, some vendors worried that shoppers would delay buying until prices fell. In practice, reduced prices applied only to items that vendors had already marked as surplus.
After six weeks, less food was going into the bins. The figures did not tell us whether vendors were making more money, because we had not collected sales records.
Next month, we will ask vendors how much time the new process takes, especially at closing time.

questions.explanation: Bread was the largest share, even though the team expected vegetables to come first.

title: Measuring shade on city streets
intro: A researcher describes how a team compared walking conditions on two streets.
dialogue: Our team wanted to know whether street trees made walking more comfortable on hot days. We chose two streets with similar building heights, but one had much more tree cover.
We first planned to take readings in the morning. We moved the measurements to the afternoon because that was when residents reported the most discomfort.
At each location, we measured both air temperature and the temperature of the pavement. The clearest difference between the streets was in pavement temperature.
We also asked pedestrians why they chose their route. Several mentioned shade, but others said they followed the street with fewer road crossings.
The survey took place in summer only. We plan to repeat it in another season before recommending where new trees should be planted.

questions.explanation: The researcher says the buildings were similar in height, but tree cover differed.

The equipment was only available then

questions.explanation: Residents said they felt most uncomfortable in the afternoon.

questions.prompt: Which measurement showed the clearest difference?
questions.explanation: The biggest difference was in the temperature of the pavement.

questions.prompt: Besides shade, what influenced some pedestrians' route choice?
questions.explanation: Some pedestrians preferred the route with fewer crossings.
